cause_claim:
The change adds GRANT SELECT ON r0.* TO svc_bundle_reader. In the candidate run, this gave svc_bundle_reader access to r0.* tables in addition to the default database, doubling the rows visible from 90 to 180. The bundle-builder produced a bundle with 180 entries, and worker-runtime refused to start because it preallocates 150 entries, observing: "bundle has 180 entries but the runtime preallocates 150; refusing to start" (exit code 2).

Evidence chain:
- Baseline experiment x-d3fae9d9456d4975: 90 rows_visible_to_builder, 90 bundle-builder.entries, worker-runtime.exit_code=0 with GRANT SELECT ON default.* only
- Candidate experiment x-e860ff8b8bf44ddf: 180 rows_visible_to_builder, 180 bundle-builder.entries, worker-runtime.exit_code=2 with both GRANT SELECT ON default.* and GRANT SELECT ON r0.* added
- Second baseline x-f808dbc5c8844234: confirmed exit_code=0 with default-only grants
- Dependency path: change → grants on database r0 → principal svc_bundle_reader → service bundle-builder → reads bundle_fields → artifact bundle.json → loaded by worker-runtime

The explicit shard grant doubles data exposure, causing the bundle size to exceed the worker-runtime preallocation limit of 150 entries.
